description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of articles across various media outlets as analyzed in the paper “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” with each slice representing the proportion of articles sourced from a specific outlet. The chart is divided into 17 segments, each labeled with the name of a media organization and its corresponding percentage share. Breitbart leads with the largest segment at 14%, followed by “Other” at 13%, and Drudge Report and The Daily Caller each at 8%. Smaller shares include The Huffington Post (7%), NPR and Vox (6% each), The Guardian and BBC (5% each), and multiple outlets tied at 3%: RT, Daily Kos, National Review, Daily Mail, Red State, Fox News, and CNN. Shareblue and PoliticusUSA each account for 3%, while the smallest segment, labeled “Other,” is not further subdivided. The slices are color-coded and arranged in descending order clockwise from the top right, with percentage values displayed inside each segment. No legend is present, and no slice is exploded or emphasized visually beyond its proportional size.
